newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-DE SILVA LEADS SRI LANKA FIGHTBACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DE SILVA LEADS SRI LANKA FIGHTBACK.

text.p: Aravinda de Silva led a Sri Lanka fightback with an unbeaten half-century against Pakistan on the fourth day of the first test on Tuesday.
De Silva hit 52 not out as Sri Lanka, 48 behind on first innings, recovered from 53 for two to 118 for two in their second innings by tea.
At the start of the day, Pakistan's final pair survived for 35 minutes before the touring side were dismissed for 378, Saqlain Mushtaq being last out for 58 in five hours.

Sri Lanka then lost Russell Arnold (15) before lunch and fellow opener Marvan Atapattu (25) soon afterwards, both to off-spinner Saqlain, the second wicket falling when they were only five runs ahead.
De Silva and captain Arjuna Ranatunga survived some anxious moments against Saqlain and leg-spinner Mustaq Ahmed as they repaired the early damage.
De Silva was harsh on fast bowler Mohammed Zahid whom he hooked for six to mid-wicket to bring up the Sri Lanka 100 in the 40th over.
The right-hander took 14 runs off that Zahid over, hitting him for two fours as well.
De Silva completed his 14th test half-century before tea by pulling Mushtaq for his sixth four, his 50 coming in 124 minutes off 98 balls.
It was the first time de Silva had reached 50 in tests since scoring 105 against Pakistan at Faisalabad in September 1995.
Ranatunga provided staunch support, and had batted 94 minutes for 19 not out at tea when the pair had added 65 for the third wicket.
